March 26, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]]. Nicknamed "'''the Arch of Dimes'''", he is widely considered among the greatest players in [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]] history. Arcidiacono was part of [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova's]] [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2016 national championship]] team, where he was awarded the [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player award]] and assisted on the game-winning basket to [[Kris Jenkins (basketball)|Kris Jenkins]] as time expired in the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|championship game]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2016/04/05/armour-villanova-win-vs-unc-will-be-remembered-as-best-title-game-ever.html|title=Villanova win vs UNC — best title game ever?|website=CNBC|date=April 5, 2016|access-date=April 5, 2016}}{{Cite web |date=April 5, 2016 |title=Villanova's Arcidiacono named Final Four MOP |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/15137291/ryan-arcidiacono-villanova-wildcats-named-final-four-mop |access-date=April 5, 2016 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} As a freshman at Villanova, Arcidiacono was named to the [[Big East Conference]] All-Rookie Team. As a junior, he was co-winner of the conference's [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Player of the Year]] award.{{cite press release|url=http://www.bigeast.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031215aaa.html |title=Rich Tradition of BIG EAST Guards Continues With Player of Year Honors For Arcidiacono and Dunn |publisher=Big East Conference |date=March 12, 2015 |access-date=March 12, 2015}} Prior to a successful college career, he attended [[Neshaminy High School]], where he averaged 20.4 points and 5.6 rebounds per game as a junior to lead Neshaminy to the [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association|PIAA]] playoffs. ==Early life== Arcidiacono was born on March 26, 1994, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He has three older siblings, Sabrina, Nicole, Michael; and younger twin siblings, Christopher and Courtney.{{cite web|title=Ryan Arcidiacono Profile|url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ryan_arcidiacono_812184.html|work=[[Villanova Wildcats]]|publisher=[[Villanova University]]|access-date=February 21, 2014|archive-date=March 31, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180331161136/http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ryan_arcidiacono_812184.html|url-status=dead}} His parents, Joe and Patti Arcidiacono, met at [[Villanova University]], where Joe was an offensive lineman on the [[Villanova Wildcats football|football team]]. His father installed a 6-foot plastic hoop in the family living room. Young Arcidiacono would often practice shooting jump shots and hitting layups on the small hoop before progressing to an actual basketball court. At one [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] game, Arcidiacono scored 50 points. At another, he hit eight [[Three-point field goal|three-pointers]] in a row. When he was in 7th grade at a basketball camp, Villanova coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]] said he would one day play for the Wildcats.{{cite news|title=Arcidiacono family 'mildly stunned' by Villanova freshman's rise|url=http://www.csnphilly.com/ncaa/arcidiacono-family-mildly-stunned-villanova-freshmans-rise|access-date=February 21, 2014|newspaper=[[Comcast SportsNet]]|date=January 11, 2013}} Growing up, his favorite athletes were the 76ers' [[Allen Iverson]] and the Eagles' [[Brian Dawkins]].{{cite news|last=Auerbach|first=Nicole|title=Villanova's Ryan Arcidiacono doesn't mind a little blood with his sweat|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigeast/2014/01/27/college-basketball-villanova-wildcats-ryan-arcidiacono/4909035/|access-date=February 21, 2014|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=January 27, 2014}} In eighth grade, Arcidiacono trained with former [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]] player Ben Luber.{{cite news|last=Jerardi|first=Dick|title=For Arch, it was all in the attitude|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/ncaa_tournament/20150319_For_Arch__it_was_all_in_the_attitude.html#QX3ZqOzDIyQRoTBX.99|access-date=April 26, 2015|newspaper=[[Philadelphia Daily News]]|date=March 19, 2015}} ==High school career== Arcidiacono attended [[Neshaminy High School]], where he was coached by Jerry Devine. Arcidiacono led the team to a [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association|PIAA]] Class AAAA tournament as a sophomore. In a playoff game against [[Bartram High School]], he tallied a [[triple-double]] of 26 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists. He averaged 18 points per game and was named to the Class AAAA second team.{{cite news|title=Liberty High School's Darrun Hilliard named first-team all-state; Chad Landis is Class AAAA co-coach of the year|url=http://www.lehighvalleylive.com/sports/index.ssf/2010/04/post_48.html|access-date=December 23, 2014|work=[[The Express-Times]]|date=April 7, 2010}} At the end of his sophomore season, Arcidiacono traveled with his AAU team, the PA Playaz, to North Carolina for the Bob Gibbons Tournament of Champions. In the first game of the tournament, he crashed into the floor face-first, an injury that required eight stitches. Despite the advice of doctors, he decided to play in the following game and responded with 35 points. He continued to score at the same pace for the remainder of the tournament, and major college programs took notice. Arcidiacono received recruiting offers from [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], and [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], among others. In October 2010, after attending Villanova's Hoops Mania event, he committed to play for the Villanova Wildcats. As a junior, Arcidiacono guided Neshaminy to a 22–7 record while averaging 20.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, 5.0 assists, and 2.2 steals.{{cite news|last=O'Brien|first=Rick|title=Neshaminy's Ryan Arcidiacono to miss basketball season|url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-12-08/sports/30490885_1_medical-procedure-minor-procedure-inquirer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301071919/http://articles.philly.com/2011-12-08/sports/30490885_1_medical-procedure-minor-procedure-inquirer|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 1, 2014|access-date=February 21, 2014|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=December 8, 2011}} He surpassed the 1,000 point mark in a game against [[Pennsbury High School|Pennsbury]], scoring 29 points in an 83–52 win.{{cite news|last=Sherman|first=Steve|title=Neshaminy's Ryan Arcidiacono surpasses 1,000 points as a junior|url=http://www.buckslocalnews.com/articles/2010/12/30/bucks_sports/doc4d12582fd842e050231448.txt|access-date=February 24, 2014|newspaper=Bucks Local News|date=December 30, 2010}} The Neshaminy Redskins reached the state quarterfinals in 2011 before losing to [[Penn Wood High School|Penn Wood]]. After his junior season, he was named the ''Bucks County Courier Times'' player of the year.{{cite news|last=Coney|first=Kevin|title=Back injury ends Arcidiacono's season before it starts|url=http://www.phillyburbs.com/sports/college/basketball/back-injury-ends-arcidiacono-s-season-before-it-starts/article_00d68bc2-1dcf-5378-af2f-5416004631bf.html?mode=jqm|access-date=February 21, 2014|newspaper=[[Bucks County Courier Times]]|date=December 9, 2011|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140221012628/http://www.phillyburbs.com/sports/college/basketball/back-injury-ends-arcidiacono-s-season-before-it-starts/article_00d68bc2-1dcf-5378-af2f-5416004631bf.html?mode=jqm|archive-date=February 21, 2014}} The ''[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]'' selected him to the first-team all-Southeastern Pennsylvania. He began to feel pain in his lower back shortly after the end of his junior season. In May 2011, while attending a basketball camp at the Deron Williams Academy in Chicago, Arcidiacono complained of poor mobility and soreness. He was diagnosed with a [[herniated disk]] in his back, forcing him to miss his senior season. Arcidiacono had surgery to repair the disk on December 21, and he could not leave his house for two weeks thereafter. Arcidiacono finished his career at Neshaminy High School as the program's all-time leading scorer. He tallied 1,498 points, 449 rebounds, 378 assists, 178 steals, and 160 three-pointers. Despite missing the season, [[ESPNU]] ranked him among the top 50 seniors in the country. ==College career== ===Freshman season (2012–2013)=== Arcidiacono began his freshman season not fully recovered from his back injury. He made his college debut scoring 11 points against the [[University of the District of Columbia]].{{cite news|title=Villanova 78, District of Columbia 58|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=323140222|access-date=March 9, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=November 9, 2012|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} In the following game against [[2012–13 Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball team|Marshall]], Arcidiacono became the first Wildcat freshman to score 25 points since [[Scottie Reynolds]]. Arcidiacono garnered his first Big East rookie of the week honors on November 18, after an 18-point six-assist performance in an overtime win against [[2012–13 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.bigeast.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111912aan.html |title=Napier, Arcidiacono Earn First Weekly Men's Basketball Honors |date=November 18, 2012 |website=[[Big East Conference]] |access-date=March 11, 2014}} He was again named Big East rookie of the week on December 31 after a 17-point performance against [[New Jersey Institute of Technology|NJIT]].{{cite web|title=Arcidiacono is BIG EAST Rookie of the Week|url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/123112aaa.html|work=[[Villanova Wildcats]]|publisher=[[Villanova University]]|access-date=March 11, 2014|date=December 31, 2012}} He had a career-high 32 points on January 2, 2013, to propel Villanova to a 98–86 overtime victory over [[2012–13 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]].{{cite news|title=Villanova 98, St. John's 86|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330020222|access-date=March 11, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=January 2, 2014|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} This performance earned Arcidiacono Big East rookie of the week honors for the week of January 6.{{cite web|title=Triche, Arcidiacono Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors|url=http://www.bigeast.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010713aam.html|work=[[Big East Conference]]|access-date=March 11, 2014|date=January 6, 2013}} In the January 26 contest against third-ranked [[2012–13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]], Arcidiacono made a 3-pointer with 2.2 seconds remaining in regulation to tie the game at 61. The Wildcats ended up defeating Syracuse in overtime 75–71.{{cite news|title=Villanova uses deep touch to upend No. 3 Syracuse in overtime|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330260222|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116083150/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330260222|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 16, 2017|access-date=March 11, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=January 26, 2013|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Arcidiacono earned his fourth rookie of the week honors in the last week of the regular season. Led by Arcidiacono, Villanova enjoyed a 20–14 season and reached the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they were seeded ninth and matched up with eighth seed [[2012–13 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the first round. Arcidiacono had 10 points, but his Wildcats lost to the Tar Heels 78–71.{{cite news|title=UNC outlasts Villanova to give Roy Williams win No. 700|access-date=March 12, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=March 22, 2013|agency=[[Associated Press]]|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330810153}} He posted averages of 11.9 points, 3.5 assists and 2.1 rebounds per game. Arcidiacono started all 34 games and played an average of 34.0 minutes per game, which led the team. He was named [[Philadelphia Big 5]] rookie of the year and was selected to the Big East All-Rookie team.{{cite news|title=A Season's Worth of Experience Aids Villanova's Ryan Arcidiacono|url=http://www.buckslocalnews.com/articles/2013/06/29/bucks_sports/doc51cef3f6acd4f825284972.txt?viewmode=fullstory|access-date=March 10, 2014|newspaper=[[Bucks Local News]]|date=June 23, 2013}} ===Sophomore season (2013–2014)=== Going into his sophomore campaign, Arcidiacono focused on improving his footwork and shooting mechanics. Arcidiacono hit a 3-pointer with 10.1 seconds left in a November 29 matchup against [[2013–14 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] despite not making a shot until that point. The Wildcats held on to upset the second-ranked Jayhawks 63–59.{{cite news|title=Villanova stuns No. 2 Kansas on late 3-pointer|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400519976|access-date=March 9, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=November 29, 2013|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Arcidiacono had his first [[double-double]] with 20 points and 11 assists in a 94–85 overtime win over [[2013–14 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] on January 25, 2014.{{cite news|title=No. 4 Villanova holds off Marquette, 94–85 in OT|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400504544|access-date=March 11, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=January 25, 2014|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} He recorded a season-high 21 points in the February 18 game against [[2013–14 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]]. With 3.1 seconds left in double overtime, Arcidiacono completed a three-point play to help the Wildcats to an 82–79 victory.{{cite news|title=No. 9 Villanova survives scare, escapes Providence in 2OT|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400504575|access-date=March 11, 2014|newspaper=[[ESPN]]|date=February 18, 2014|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} He was an honorable mention all-Big East selection after the regular season.{{cite news|last=Toohey|first=Terry|title=Villanova senior James Bell named Big East first team all-conference|url=https://www.mainlinemedianews.com/2014/03/09/villanova-senior-james-bell-named-big-east-first-team-all-conference/|access-date=August 30, 2022|newspaper=Main Line Media News|date=March 9, 2014}} He joined teammate [[Darrun Hilliard]] on the All-Big 5 Second Team.{{cite news|last=Jensen|first=Mike|title=Big Five Hall of Famers honored with current stars|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/20140415_Big_Five_Hall_of_Famers_honored_with_current_stars.html#HWkeVs2pEU5VpJaI.99|access-date=April 15, 2014|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=April 15, 2014}} He posted averages of 9.9 points, 3.5 assists and 2.4 rebounds per contest. Arcidiacono started 33 games and played an average of 31.1 minutes per game, leading the team. ===Junior season (2014–2015)=== Arcidiacono was selected to the preseason second team All-Big East.{{cite men's basketball team|Creighton]].{{cite news|title=Ryan Arcidiacono saves No. 4 Villanova against Creighton|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400588477|access-date=April 2015|newspaper=[[Philadelphia Daily News]]|date=March 15, 2015}} After overcoming a nagging right wrist injury in December, Arcidiacono averaged 12.9 points and 3.6 assists and made 45.5 percent of his attempts from the floor and 44.4 percent from the three-point arc in Big East conference play. He shared Big East Player of the Year honors with Providence guard [[Kris Dunn]], feeling "kind of shocked" about the selection.{{cite news|last=Juliano|first=Joe|title=Arcidiacono is Big East co-player of the year|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/20150312_Arcidiacono_is_Big_East_co-player_of_the_year.html#zkpFFsrwum2jf4pI.99|access-date=April 26, 2015|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=March 12, 2015}} Arcidiacono was a 2014–15 Men's All-District II Team selection by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|U.S. Basketball Writers Association]].{{cite web| url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2015/alldistrict150310.html| work=[[United States Basketball Writers Association]]| title=USBWA Names 2014-15 Men's All-District Teams| access-date=April 26, 2015|date=March 10, 2015}} He was named to the Second Team All-District V by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nabc.org/awards/all_district/2014-15_NABC_Division_I_All-District_Teams_and_Coaches-2.pdf|title=National Association of Basketball Coaches Announces: 2014-15 Division I All-District Teams and UPS All-District Coaches|access-date=April 8, 2015|date=March 27, 2015|publisher=[[National Association of Basketball Coaches]]}} He was named to the All-Big 5 First Team.{{cite news|last=O'Brien|first=Rick|title=College Basketball: Lower Merion's B.J. |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/villanova-wildcats/former-villanova-star-ryan-arcidiacono-joining-pro-team-italy |access-date=February 13, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=July 10, 2017}} On February 12, 2020, he had his number 15 jersey retired at Villanova.{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=K.C. |date=February 12, 2020 |title=Bulls guard Ryan Arcidiacono relishes Villanova honor as 'really special' |work=[[NBC Sports]] |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/bulls-guard-ryan-arcidiacono-relishes-villanova-honor-really-special |access-date=February 13, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Austin Spurs (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Arcidiacono joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2016-utah-summer-league-roster/|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2016 UTAH SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2016|access-date=January 3, 2017}} On July 14, 2016, he signed with the Spurs,{{cite web|title=SAN ANTONIO SIGNS RYAN ARCIDIACONO|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/san-antonio-signs-ryan-arcidiacono|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}} but was waived on October 22 after appearing in three preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-waive-joel-anthony-ryan-arcidiacono-patricio-garino-and-livio-jean-charles|title=SPURS WAIVE JOEL ANTHONY, RYAN ARCIDIACONO, PATRICIO GARINO AND LIVIO JEAN-CHARLES|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}} Seven days later, he was acquired by the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate of San Antonio.{{cite web|url=http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2016-returning-players-training-camp-invitees/|title=AUSTIN SPURS ANNOUNCE 2016 RETURNING PLAYERS AND TRAINING CAMP INVITEES|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016|archive-date=January 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170114123755/http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2016-returning-players-training-camp-invitees/|url-status=dead}} For the 2017–18 season, Arcidiacono originally signed with the Italian team [[Juvecaserta Basket]].{{cite web | title = Firmanto Ryan Arcidiacono | work = [[Juvecaserta Basket]] | date = July 6, 2017 | url = http://www.juvecaserta.it/juvecaserta/2017/07/06/firmato-ryan-arcidiacono/ | access-date = July 6, 2017 | language = it-IT | archive-date = December 18, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171218211932/http://www.juvecaserta.it/juvecaserta/2017/07/06/firmato-ryan-arcidiacono/ | url-status = dead }} However, on July 14, 2017, it was announced that Juvecaserta would not be accepted in Serie A, as it was rejected by Com.Tec. (Commission of control on the companies' financial statements). As a result, he voided the contract with the Italian company.{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/it/italia/serie-a/241194/le-decisioni-del-consiglio-federale-la-pasta-reggia-caserta-non-ammessa-al-campionato-di-serie-a.html|title=Le decisioni del Consiglio Federale: la Pasta Reggia Caserta non ammessa al campionato di Serie A|work=Sportando|access-date=August 1, 2017|language=it-IT}} ===Chicago Bulls (2017–2021)=== On July 25, 2017, Arcidiacono signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Chicago Bulls,{{Cite news|url=http://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/bulls-sign-point-guard-ryan-arcidiacono-to-a-two-way-contract/|title=Bulls sign point guard Ryan Arcidiacono to a two-way contract|work=Chicago Sun-Times|access-date=August 1, 2017}} the team he played with the [[2017 NBA Summer League]] in Las Vegas{{Cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-announce-2017-summer-league-roster/|title=Bulls announce 2017 Summer League Roster {{!}} Chicago Bulls|work=Chicago Bulls|access-date=August 1, 2017}} As a result, he would split time between Chicago and their G League affiliate, the [[Windy City Bulls]] throughout the season, with Arcidiacono spending most of his time out in the Windy City. He also became the first player in franchise history to sign a two-way deal. After playing sparingly with Chicago, Arcidiacono averaged 13.8 points, 5 rebounds, and 8.6 assists per game with Windy City. He posted 7.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, and four assists per game in the 2018 NBA Summer League with Chicago. On July 31, 2018, Arcidiacono signed a standard contract with the Bulls.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/07/31/chicago-bulls-re-sign-guard-ryan-arcidiacono |title=Chicago Bulls re-sign guard Ryan Arcidiacono |agency=Associated Press |website=NBA |access-date=August 21, 2018}} On October 18, he recorded eight points, four rebounds and a career-high eight assists in the season-opener against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.vuhoops.com/2018/10/18/17998758/nba-villanova-wildcats-watch-october-18-2018-recap-highlights-stats-bulls-lakers-hart-arcidiacono|title=NBA Wildcat Watch (October 18)|last=Warren|first=Steve|date=October 18, 2018|work=VU Hoops}} With three starters injured early in the season, he started to see an increase in playing time. On November 26, 2018, Arcidiacono scored a career-high 22 points with four rebounds, two assists and two steals in a 107–108 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070978 |title=Aldridge helps Spurs beat Bulls 108-107 |agency=Associated Press |date=November 26, 2018 |work=ESPN |access-date=November 26, 2018}} On July 2, 2019, Arcidiacono signed a three-year contract with the Bulls.{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/bulls/ct-bulls-re-sign-ryan-arcidiacono-20190702-jbfrore3k5g7fezlvpmswcs6ba-jbfrore3k5g7fezlvpmswcs6ba-story.html|title=Bulls reach terms with Ryan Arcidiacono on a 3-year, $9 million deal and get a commitment from free-agent big man Luke Kornet|last=Johnson|first=K. C.|date=July 2, 2019|website=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=February 13, 2020}} ===Maine Celtics (2021–2022)=== On September 28, 2021, Arcidiacono signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/boston-celtics-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 16.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Celtics Release Ryan Arcidiacono, Juwan with the [[Maine Celtics]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Celtics Acquire Two In Draft, Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/draft-camp-102321/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On January 6, 2022, Arcidiacono signed a 10-day contract with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|date=January 6, 2022|title=Knicks Sign Ryan Arcidiacono to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-ryan-arcidiacono-10-day-contract|access-date=January 6, 2022|website=NBA.com}} On January 13, without appearing in a game, Arcidiacono was waived by the Knicks.{{cite web|date=January 13, 2022|title=Knicks Acquire Cam Reddish|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-acquire-cam-reddish|access-date=January 14, 2022|website=NBA.com}}{{cite web|last1=Stinar|first1=Ben|date=January 14, 2022|title=The New York Knicks Have Waived A 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220114155903/https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/the-new-york-knicks-and-atlanta-hawks-made-a-multi-player-trade-on-friday-and-they-also-waived-ryan-arcidiacono|url-status=dead}} On January 19, Arcidiacono signed a standard 10-day contract with the team, but didn't play a game for them again.{{cite web|date=January 19, 2022|title=Knicks Sign Ryan Arcidiacono to 10-Day York Knicks (2022–2023)=== On February 13, Arcidiacono was signed by the [[New York Knicks]] for the rest of the 2021–22 season.{{cite web |title=Knicks Sign Ryan Arcidiacono |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-ryan-arcidiacono |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 14, 2022 |date=February 13, 2022}} On September 17, 2022, Arcidiacono re-signed ===Portland Trail Blazers (2023)=== On February 9, 2023, the Knicks reached an agreement to trade Arcidiacono, [[Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk]], [[Cam Reddish]] and draft considerations to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for [[Josh Hart]], Arcidiacono's former teammate at Villanova.{{cite news|first=Jack|last=Maloney|title=Josh Hart-Cam Reddish trade grades: Solid move for Knicks; Blazers take sellers' stance|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/josh-hart-cam-reddish-trade-grades-solid-move-for-knicks-blazers-take-sellers-stance/|website=CBSSports.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=April 1, 2023}} The deal was completed as a four-team trade involving the [[Charlotte Hornets]] and [[Philadelphia 76ers]], with the Hornets receiving Mykhailiuk, the 76ers receiving [[Jalen McDaniels]], the Knicks receiving Hart and the Trail Blazers receiving Arcidiacono, Reddish and [[Matisse Thybulle]].{{Cite web |date=February 9, 2023 |title=Portland Completes Multi-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/portland-completes-multi-team-trade |access-date=February 9, 2023 |website=NBA}} On April 1, Arcidiacono was waived by the Trail Blazers.{{cite web | title=Trail Blazers Sign Jeenathan Williams | website=NBA.com | date=2023-04-01 | url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-jeenathan-williams | access-date=2024-12-26}} ===Return to the Knicks (2023–2024)=== On September 15, 2023, Arcidiacono signed with the New York Knicks, returning to the franchise for a second stint.{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Ryan Arcidiacono|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-ryan-arcidiacono-2|website=NBA.com|date=September 15, 2023|access-date=February 10, 2024}} During his second stint with the Knicks, Arcidiacono set an NBA record for the most consecutive games played without scoring a single point, failing to score in 20 consecutive games.{{cite web|first=DJ|last=Dunson|title=The Knicks and Ryan Arcidiacono are the cure to the NBA’s scoring surge|url=https://deadspin.com/ryan-arcidiacono-ny-knicks-tom-thibodeau-nba-1851230937|website=Deadspin.com|date=February 6, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} On February 8, 2024, Arcidiacono, [[Malachi Flynn]], [[Evan Fournier]], [[Quentin Grimes]] and two second-round picks were traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Bojan Bogdanović]] and [[Alec Burks]].{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS ACQUIRE QUENTIN GRIMES, EVAN FOURNIER, MALACHI FLYNN, RYAN ARCIDIACONO, TWO FUTURE SECOND ROUND DRAFT PICKS AND CASH CONSIDERATIONS FROM NEW
